title: A prospective theory that predicts mammalian circuit computation from connectivity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a theory that takes a mammalian circuit’s measured wiring and cell identities, together with explicitly stated information about its inputs and biological context, and predicts what computation the circuit performs. Before new functional experiments, it would predict how individual neurons respond and how specified interventions change circuit activity and behavior. The central advance would be discovering an unfamiliar circuit’s computation prospectively, rather than constructing an explanation after its function is known.

Connectivity constrains possible mechanisms but need not uniquely determine function: circuits with the same wiring can function differently. A successful theory must therefore specify which additional constraints it needs and which conclusions follow from them. The documented fly work provides an important foundation by combining connectivity with a supplied computational task to predict neural responses. That achievement differs from identifying the task itself from anatomical and biological constraints.

Neural coding, a possible canonical computation of cortical columns, and the biological representation of semantic meaning are related questions. They could inform this theory or become domains in which it is tested. The supplied tertiary problem list identifies these questions, but does not establish that there is one universal spike code or that all three questions require a single unified solution.

significance.text: If demonstrated, this capability would substantially strengthen the predictive and causal use of circuit anatomy. An experimenter could use a measured circuit to formulate advance predictions about its computation, neuron-level responses, and the behavioral effects of changing a defined cell class. The distinction matters because reproducing responses while training for an already specified task does not establish that the task could have been discovered from the circuit. The fly study demonstrates the value of detailed, experimentally testable predictions while retaining that task constraint.

Conditional significance: reliable intervention predictions could help researchers choose experiments, distinguish competing mechanisms, and identify which circuit elements are responsible for particular transformations. Successful prediction across unfamiliar mammalian circuits would provide evidence that the theory captures transferable principles rather than an explanation tailored to one pathway. These benefits depend on the breadth and accuracy of prospective validation.

Semantic or conceptual transformations would enter the demonstrated scope only when the relevant variables and transformations were explicitly defined and prospectively tested. Predicting one abstract variable would be meaningful progress, but would not establish a general account of meaning, all conceptual thought, or a universal neural code. Likewise, success in a small number of circuits would support bounded generalization rather than literal universality.

Conditional downstream possibilities include better circuit models for clinical intervention, reconstruction, and eventually larger-scale emulation. Whole-brain emulation, content-faithful memory access, communication between minds, and an account of conscious experience would each require additional advances in measurement, intervention, validation, or theory. Engineered creativity and machine super-intelligence would be still further possibilities, not direct consequences established by a predictive circuit theory.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability defined by this proposal is prospective identification of unfamiliar mammalian circuit computations, coupled to accurate predictions of specified perturbations. Connectivity alone can leave multiple functional mechanisms possible, while supplying a task constrains the model using information about the computation being explained. The theory must bridge that gap without silently importing the target function through training objectives, functional measurements, or model selection.

Engineering synthesis: the theory needs an explicit account of which biological quantities must be measured, which can be inferred, and which remain uncertain. Wiring and cell identity may leave unknown parameters that affect circuit dynamics. Inputs, operating context, and circuit boundaries must also be specified well enough to distinguish a wrong computational theory from an incomplete description of the system. A useful prediction should expose these dependencies rather than treat an anatomical map as a complete functional specification.

Scientific synthesis: predicting an intervention requires more than matching ordinary activity. A model must capture causal dependencies well enough to predict the consequences of silencing a cell class, including any effect on behavior under defined conditions. This creates a separate validation burden: agreement with unperturbed neural responses does not by itself establish accurate predictions after intervention.

Evaluation synthesis: an unfamiliar circuit’s computation must be described in a form that can be tested independently. For an abstract or semantic variable, investigators must define the variable, the behavioral task, and the predicted transformation precisely enough to separate conceptual representation from correlated sensory or motor signals. They must also control training leakage and declare allowable prior task knowledge. These are concrete requirements for testing the proposed capability, not evidence that a particular universal theory exists.

current_state.text: In 2024, Lappalainen, Tschopp, Prakhya, and colleagues reported a connectome-constrained model in Nature 634, pages 1132–1140, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07939-3. It used connectivity for 64 cell types in fly visual motion pathways and optimized unknown parameters for a supplied visual-motion task, specifically optic-flow estimation. The authors reported agreement between model predictions and neural activity measurements across 26 previously published studies.

The construction of this model used connectome and task constraints without fitting neural activity measurements. Its agreement with recorded responses is therefore a substantive predictive achievement, and should not be described as merely fitting published activity. Nevertheless, the computational objective was supplied in advance, the circuit was a fly pathway, and the comparisons involved existing studies. The result does not demonstrate prospective discovery of an unfamiliar mammalian circuit’s computation. Some subsequent mechanistic analyses also selected models using known tuning, which limits how independently those analyses can be interpreted.

The supplied review assessed the full primary-article text, but did not independently inspect the underlying 26 studies or figure images. The quantitative account above is consequently an account of the authors’ reported findings as evaluated in that review, rather than an independent replication or reanalysis. This limitation does not invalidate the reported result.

The supplied evidence does not establish field-wide achievement or non-achievement of the proposed capability as of 1 November 2026: the review contains no bounded freshness search. The Wikipedia copy was retrieved on 11 November 2026 and reportedly showed a 30 October edit; those dates do not establish the scientific state at the cutoff. Its list of questions is useful orientation, not an authoritative survey proving that every related problem remains unsolved.

An additional supplied book PDF yielded identifiable front matter and contents, but the review reported extraction problems and no substantive chapter text adequate to resolve the theoretical questions. It therefore cannot establish the current state of a general circuit theory. The supplied materials also do not substantiate the earlier specific assertions about MICrONS measurement volume or speech and inner-speech decoder capabilities; those assertions cannot serve as demonstrated milestones in this record.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: test at least two mammalian circuits whose functions were not used to train or select the model. Before collecting the new functional data, preregister the predicted computation, single-neuron response classes, and behavioral consequences of silencing one defined cell class in each circuit. Compare the predictions with subsequent experiments. Two circuits are a proposed initial test of transfer, not a source-established threshold for completing the field.
completion_criteria.label: Validate preregistered functional and silencing predictions across two unfamiliar circuits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safeguards: specify the permitted anatomical information, cell identities, contextual inputs, and prior task knowledge before prediction. Document training data and model-selection decisions so that functional information cannot enter indirectly. Define quantitative success thresholds, uncertainty estimates, and comparison models in advance. A task-conditioned model may be a useful comparator, while the central test must determine what the theory predicts when the target computation has not been supplied.
completion_criteria.label: Predefine information safeguards and evaluation without supplying target computation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth test: include at least one circuit carrying an operationally defined abstract or semantic variable, with experiments designed to distinguish that variable from correlated sensory inputs or motor outputs. This would extend the demonstration beyond a sensory reflex. It would establish performance on the tested variable and transformation, not general access to meaning or all unspoken conceptual thought.
completion_criteria.label: Distinguish abstract or semantic variables from sensorimotor correlates experimentally

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: make the model, prediction procedure, data provenance, and experimental protocols sufficiently accessible for independent groups to repeat the analysis and test new animals or circuits. Report anatomical completeness, measurement uncertainty, required biological inputs, and the conditions under which predictions fail. A convincing result should include both activity and perturbation outcomes. Finite tests establish demonstrated breadth; they cannot prove a universal neural code or unrestricted applicability across mammalian brains.
completion_criteria.label: Enable independent replication and report biological requirements and limitations

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NEU-01, simultaneous spike-resolved recording from every neuron in a behaving mammalian brain, concerns functional measurement; NEU-02, routine synaptic-resolution connectomics of entire mammalian brains, concerns structural measurement. Both could provide inputs or validation data for NEU-03, whose distinct objective is to infer computation and intervention effects. A complete recording or wiring map would not, by itself, constitute that explanatory and predictive theory. The supplied review does not establish specific MICrONS achievements.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-04 concerns content-faithful reading and writing of specific episodic memories. A theory of relevant circuits could help explain memory transformations, but predicting circuit computation would not automatically provide memory-specific read and write access. NEU-07 concerns noninvasive cellular-resolution read and write through the intact adult human skull, while NEU-09 concerns cell-type-specific molecular access throughout the intact adult human brain. These are access and intervention capabilities that could enable tests of NEU-03; their technical objectives remain distinct from the theory.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-05 concerns target-specific regrowth of long axons in the adult mammalian central nervous system, and NEU-06 concerns reconstruction of human cognitive circuits after neuronal loss. NEU-03 could potentially help specify the functional consequences of a proposed repair. It would not itself supply axon guidance, replace lost neurons, or demonstrate restoration of cognition.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-08, a generative developmental code that builds a specified functional neural circuit, approaches the structure–function relationship through construction. NEU-03 approaches it through prediction from a measured circuit. The two could inform one another, but predicting what an existing circuit does does not establish how to build it. NEU-11, reversible and circuit-specific reopening of critical-period plasticity in adults, concerns control of circuit change; a predictive theory might help anticipate that change without supplying the biological means to induce it.

Roster-based synthesis: NEU-10 seeks a causal, measurement-grade account of conscious content. NEU-03 could explain computations associated with a defined content, but that would not alone establish an account of consciousness. NEU-12 seeks a sufficient account of sleep that allows its necessary brain functions to be completed without a normal sleep period. Circuit predictions might contribute to understanding particular sleep functions, while replacing the necessary functions of sleep would require additional explanation and intervention.

change_log.change: Preserved NEU-03 and its title while defining the innovation around prospective mammalian computation and perturbation prediction.
change_log.reason: This retains the candidate’s identity and central scientific ambition without presenting the proposed capability as achieved.

change_log.change: Added explicit assumptions about inputs, biological context, unknown parameters, and circuit boundaries.
change_log.reason: The review establishes that connectivity need not uniquely determine function; the proposed theory must identify its additional constraints.

change_log.change: Reframed neural coding, canonical cortical computation, and semantic representation as related questions rather than necessary components of one universal theory.
change_log.reason: The supplied sources do not establish their necessary unification or the existence of a universal spike code.

change_log.change: Retained the 2024 fly result’s 64 cell types and comparison with 26 studies, and specified task optimization for optic-flow estimation.
change_log.reason: These details are supported by the reviewed primary article and clarify the demonstrated scope.

change_log.change: Corrected the description of model fitting and distinguished construction from later mechanistic model selection.
change_log.reason: Construction used no neural activity measurements; some subsequent analyses used known tuning. Calling the entire result a fit to recorded activity would obscure its predictive achievement.

change_log.change: Removed unsupported MICrONS and decoder performance assertions from the demonstrated milestones while retaining relevant conceptual relationships.
change_log.reason: The supplied texts do not substantiate those results. The roster also identifies NEU-04 specifically with episodic memory access.

change_log.reason: These review recommendations make the proposed demonstration assessable while preserving its status as a proposal and limiting conclusions to tested breadth.

change_log.change: Preserved primary-study inspection limits and the book PDF’s extraction limitations.
change_log.reason: These affect what the supplied review can establish without implying that unverified or inaccessible evidence is false.

change_log.reason: Circuit prediction could support other advances without completing their distinct measurement, access, repair, developmental, or explanatory objectives.

unresolved_issues: Whether the proposed capability had been demonstrated anywhere in neuroscience by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because the supplied review contains no bounded freshness search.
The necessary biological inputs beyond connectivity and cell identity, and the degree to which computation is identifiable from those inputs, remain unspecified.
Quantitative success thresholds, circuit selection, allowable prior task knowledge, and the definition of an abstract or semantic variable still require an experimental protocol.
The underlying 26 activity studies and figure images were not independently inspected in the supplied review; independent replication is not established by this record.
The supplied materials cannot establish the earlier MICrONS and speech or inner-speech decoder claims, and the book PDF extraction cannot resolve the broader theoretical questions.
Whether transferable principles require a universal code or canonical cortical computation remains open; the supplied evidence does not establish that such unification is necessary.
